**Why multi-head attention instead of a single head**

The Harvard diagram (the-annotated-transformer_14_0.png) shows each encoder/decoder block containing a "Multi-Head Attention" box, matching Figure 1 on paper page 3, where the encoder's first sub-layer is "a multi-head self-attention mechanism" and the decoder adds "multi-head attention over the encoder's output" (Vaswani et al., 2017, p. 3). The paper's page 4 explanation states: "Instead of performing a single attention function with d_model-dimensional keys, values and queries, we found it beneficial to linearly project the queries, keys and values h times with different, learned linear projections... we then perform the attention function in parallel" (p. 4, §3.2.2). Multiple heads let the model attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions simultaneously—a single averaged head would suppress this diversity.

**Sources:** Vaswani et al., *Attention Is All You Need*, arXiv:1706.03762, pp. 1, 3–4; Harvard NLP, *The Annotated Transformer*.
